ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ella Fitzgerald

code.originalText: Two-week review: glucose and hypoglycemia safety on the new plan, and vascular surgery consultation

text.paragraph: Two-week review of the new glucose plan, seen the same day by vascular surgery. [S]

Ms. Fitzgerald returns two weeks after her first visit and is seen by Dr. Okafor-Lane of vascular surgery on the same day. She stopped glipizide, moved glargine 24 units to the morning, and started empagliflozin 10 mg and atorvastatin 80 mg. Her continuous glucose monitor shows glucose between 70 and 180 mg/dL 58% of the time, time below 70 mg/dL 0.5%, with a lowest reading of 68 mg/dL after a long rehearsal, and no reading below 54 mg/dL; there have been no lows after shows. She has no burning or itching with urination and no muscle aches. Calf cramping still stops her after about one and a half blocks, more on the right; she has no rest pain or sores. Her right eye remains blurred; the retina clinic will see her next week. [S]

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes with peripheral artery disease (E11.51). No lows below 54 mg/dL since glipizide was stopped and glargine was reduced and moved to the morning. Time in range is 58%; the usual goal is above 70%, or above 50% for an older adult at high risk of lows, and it should rise as empagliflozin takes effect. Dr. Okafor-Lane's arterial duplex shows an occluded right superficial femoral artery with flow restored above the knee and two open arteries to the foot, and a 50 to 69% narrowing of the left superficial femoral artery; no disease above the groin. She has lifestyle-limiting claudication without signs of a threatened limb, so supervised exercise and medicines come first. [S]
Start rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily with aspirin 81 mg.
Supervised exercise three times a week for twelve weeks, starting next week, with a home walking plan for tour weeks.
No procedure now; vascular review of revascularization after twelve weeks of exercise, sooner for rest pain, a wound, or color change.
Podiatry appointment within three weeks.

Diabetic macular edema, right eye (E11.3311). Retina clinic appointment next week to start anti-VEGF injections. [S]
Keep the retina appointment.
